chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who fasts during the journey out of ignorance, does not make it up.

key_terms.قَضَى: to make up (a missed obligatory act)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up a fast if one fasts while traveling out of ignorance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for a traveler who fasts out of ignorance (jahala), establishing that their fast is valid and no make-up (qada) is required, distinguishing it from cases of deliberate violation. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that ignorance of a ruling can mitigate the obligation of re-performance, emphasizing mercy in legal application. The ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law regarding travelers, balancing spiritual discipline with practical ease.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who Fasts during the journey out of ignorance, would not make up for it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who fasts on a journey because of ignorance is not required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast)/”
